mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone, cutting renal potassium excretion; added dietary potassium or salt substitutes can cause hyperkalaemia.
dietary_guidance: Avoid potassium-based salt substitutes; keep high-potassium foods consistent, not loaded.

mechanism: High sodium intake blunts the blood-pressure-lowering effect of ACE inhibitors.
dietary_guidance: Moderate salt intake supports blood-pressure control.

mechanism: Glycyrrhizin causes sodium retention and potassium loss (pseudo-aldosteronism), opposing blood-pressure control.
dietary_guidance: Avoid regular licorice / mulethi-containing products.

mechanism: ARBs blunt aldosterone-driven potassium excretion; extra dietary potassium risks hyperkalaemia.
dietary_guidance: Avoid potassium salt substitutes; keep high-potassium foods steady.

mechanism: High sodium reduces ARB antihypertensive efficacy.
dietary_guidance: Keep salt intake moderate.

mechanism: Pseudo-aldosteronism from glycyrrhizin opposes blood-pressure control.
dietary_guidance: Avoid licorice / mulethi.

mechanism: These agents directly retain potassium; added dietary potassium risks dangerous hyperkalaemia.
dietary_guidance: Avoid salt substitutes and potassium supplements; do not load high-potassium foods.

mechanism: Ciclosporin and tacrolimus reduce potassium excretion and can cause hyperkalaemia.
dietary_guidance: Avoid potassium salt substitutes; keep potassium intake steady.

mechanism: High dietary potassium works against the purpose of potassium-binding therapy.
dietary_guidance: Follow a potassium-restricted diet as directed.

mechanism: High sodium intake counteracts thiazide-induced natriuresis and blood-pressure lowering.
dietary_guidance: Keep salt intake moderate.

mechanism: Glycyrrhizin-induced potassium loss is additive with thiazide hypokalaemia; risk of arrhythmia.
dietary_guidance: Avoid licorice / mulethi entirely.

mechanism: Thiazides reduce urinary calcium excretion; very high calcium intake can cause hypercalcaemia.
dietary_guidance: Avoid high-dose calcium supplements unless advised.

mechanism: High sodium intake offsets loop-diuretic effect on fluid overload and blood pressure.
dietary_guidance: Follow the prescribed sodium restriction.

mechanism: Additive potassium loss with loop-diuretic hypokalaemia.
dietary_guidance: Avoid licorice / mulethi.

mechanism: Both cause sodium retention and potassium loss; combined effect can be marked.
dietary_guidance: Avoid licorice / mulethi during steroid courses.

mechanism: Licorice-induced hypokalaemia sensitises the myocardium to digoxin, precipitating toxicity.
dietary_guidance: Avoid licorice / mulethi; report palpitations.

mechanism: Grapefruit furanocoumarins inhibit intestinal CYP3A4, raising simvastatin/atorvastatin levels and myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk.
dietary_guidance: Avoid grapefruit and pomelo (esp. with simvastatin/atorvastatin).

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition raises dihydropyridine levels, causing excessive hypotension and oedema.
dietary_guidance: Avoid grapefruit and pomelo.

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition raises verapamil/diltiazem levels; bradycardia and hypotension.
dietary_guidance: Avoid grapefruit and pomelo.

mechanism: Strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition markedly raises tacrolimus/ciclosporin/sirolimus levels; nephrotoxicity.
dietary_guidance: Avoid grapefruit, pomelo and Seville orange completely.

mechanism: CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition raises colchicine to toxic levels; colchicine toxicity can be fatal.
dietary_guidance: Avoid grapefruit and pomelo while taking colchicine.

mechanism: Amiodarone/dronedarone levels rise with CYP3A4 inhibition; QT prolongation.
dietary_guidance: Avoid grapefruit and pomelo.

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition raises ergot levels; risk of ergotism (vasospasm).
dietary_guidance: Avoid grapefruit and pomelo.

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition raises sildenafil/tadalafil levels; hypotension, headache.
dietary_guidance: Separate from grapefruit/pomelo intake.

mechanism: Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4/P-gp, modestly raising apixaban/rivaroxaban exposure and bleeding risk.
dietary_guidance: Avoid large or regular grapefruit/pomelo intake.

mechanism: Additive CYP3A4 inhibition (clarithromycin/erythromycin) with grapefruit.
dietary_guidance: Avoid grapefruit during the course.

mechanism: Grapefruit reduces OATP-mediated uptake of fexofenadine, lowering its effect.
dietary_guidance: Take fexofenadine with water, not fruit juice.

mechanism: Dietary vitamin K antagonises warfarin; fluctuating intake destabilises INR and can cause clot or bleed.
dietary_guidance: Keep leafy-green / vitamin-K intake CONSISTENT day to day; do not binge or eliminate.

mechanism: Acute alcohol raises INR (reduced metabolism); chronic use lowers it (enzyme induction).
dietary_guidance: Limit and keep alcohol intake steady; avoid binge drinking.

mechanism: Grapefruit can raise warfarin exposure and INR.
dietary_guidance: Avoid regular grapefruit/pomelo.

mechanism: Additive gastrointestinal bleeding risk.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol.

mechanism: Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4 activation of clopidogrel to its active metabolite, reducing antiplatelet effect.
dietary_guidance: Avoid grapefruit with clopidogrel.

mechanism: NSAIDs promote sodium and fluid retention, raising blood pressure and opposing antihypertensives.
dietary_guidance: Keep salt intake low if using NSAIDs regularly.

mechanism: Additive gastric mucosal injury; significant upper-GI bleeding risk.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol while taking NSAIDs.

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal potassium excretion; hyperkalaemia risk, especially with RAAS drugs.
dietary_guidance: Avoid potassium salt substitutes.

mechanism: Sodium/fluid retention as with non-selective NSAIDs.
dietary_guidance: Keep salt intake moderate.

mechanism: GI bleeding risk lower than non-selective NSAIDs but still additive.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol.

mechanism: Mineralocorticoid activity causes sodium and fluid retention; oedema and raised blood pressure.
dietary_guidance: Follow a lower-salt diet during steroid therapy.

mechanism: Corticosteroids raise blood glucose (steroid-induced hyperglycaemia); added sugar compounds it.
dietary_guidance: Limit sugary foods and drinks during steroid courses, especially if diabetic.

mechanism: High-glycaemic carbohydrate worsens steroid-induced hyperglycaemia.
dietary_guidance: Prefer low-GI carbohydrates during steroid therapy.

mechanism: Additive gastric irritation and immunosuppression; blood-glucose swings.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol.

mechanism: Long-term steroids reduce bone density; adequate dietary calcium and vitamin D are PROTECTIVE, not harmful.
dietary_guidance: Maintain adequate calcium and vitamin D intake - this is beneficial, not a restriction.

mechanism: Alcohol increases the risk of lactic acidosis with metformin and can cause delayed hypoglycaemia.
dietary_guidance: Avoid binge drinking; take metformin with food.

mechanism: Added sugar directly opposes glycaemic control.
dietary_guidance: Limit free sugars; match carbohydrate to the meal plan.

mechanism: High-GI carbohydrate causes glucose spikes that metformin cannot fully offset.
dietary_guidance: Prefer low-GI carbohydrate sources.

mechanism: Alcohol potentiates sulfonylurea hypoglycaemia; some (e.g. glibenclamide) can give a disulfiram-like flush.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol, especially on an empty stomach.

mechanism: Added sugar opposes glycaemic control and complicates dose titration.
dietary_guidance: Limit free sugars.

mechanism: Alcohol blocks hepatic gluconeogenesis, causing delayed hypoglycaemia hours after drinking.
dietary_guidance: If drinking, do so with food and monitor glucose; avoid binge drinking.
example_drugs: insulin glargine, insulin aspart, human insulin

mechanism: Free sugars cause rapid glucose spikes requiring careful bolus matching.
dietary_guidance: Count carbohydrate; limit sugary drinks.

mechanism: High-GI carbohydrate can outpace rapid-acting insulin.
dietary_guidance: Prefer low-GI carbohydrate; adjust timing with clinician.

mechanism: Added sugar opposes glycaemic control.
dietary_guidance: Limit free sugars.

mechanism: Added sugar opposes glycaemic control.
dietary_guidance: Limit free sugars.

mechanism: Alcohol plus SGLT2 inhibition raises the risk of (euglycaemic) diabetic ketoacidosis and volume depletion.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol; stay hydrated.

mechanism: Added sugar opposes post-prandial glucose control.
dietary_guidance: Limit free sugars; take drug with meals.

mechanism: Fluid retention is a class effect; high sodium worsens oedema and heart-failure risk.
dietary_guidance: Keep salt intake low.

mechanism: Delays sucrose digestion; also, hypoglycaemia on these drugs must be treated with GLUCOSE, not table sugar.
dietary_guidance: Limit sucrose; carry glucose tablets for hypos.

mechanism: Linezolid is a reversible MAO inhibitor; tyramine-rich foods can precipitate a hypertensive reaction.
dietary_guidance: Avoid aged cheese, fermented soy, tap/'draught' beer, cured meats and yeast extracts.

mechanism: MAO inhibition impairs histamine breakdown; fermented/aged foods can trigger flushing and headache.
dietary_guidance: Avoid fermented and aged foods during the course.

mechanism: Additive pressor effect with large caffeine loads.
dietary_guidance: Limit caffeine during linezolid therapy.

mechanism: Isoniazid has weak MAO-inhibitory activity; large tyramine loads can cause a pressor reaction.
dietary_guidance: Avoid aged cheese and fermented foods with isoniazid-containing regimens.

mechanism: Isoniazid inhibits diamine oxidase; histamine-rich fish (tuna, mackerel) can cause a scombroid-like reaction.
dietary_guidance: Avoid poorly-stored or histamine-rich fish with isoniazid.

mechanism: Additive hepatotoxicity with isoniazid/rifampicin/pyrazinamide.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol for the duration of TB therapy.

mechanism: TCAs are not MAO inhibitors; tyramine interaction is minor compared with MAOIs but a mild pressor potentiation is described.
dietary_guidance: No strict restriction; very large tyramine loads best avoided.

mechanism: Clinically insignificant with SSRIs (unlike MAOIs); listed to document that no tyramine diet is needed.
dietary_guidance: No tyramine restriction required.

mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression; risk of oversedation and death.
dietary_guidance: Do not drink alcohol while taking benzodiazepines.

mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression; complex sleep behaviours.
dietary_guidance: Do not drink alcohol.

mechanism: Additive CNS/respiratory depression with a narrow safety margin.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol entirely.

mechanism: Additive respiratory depression and sedation; overdose risk.
dietary_guidance: Do not drink alcohol while taking opioids.

mechanism: Additive CNS depression and dizziness.
dietary_guidance: Avoid or strictly limit alcohol.

mechanism: Additive sedation and psychomotor impairment.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol.

mechanism: Caffeine can mask sedation without removing impairment.
dietary_guidance: Do not rely on caffeine to offset drowsiness.

mechanism: Additive sedation, hypotension and impaired coordination.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol.

mechanism: Class-related weight gain and metabolic syndrome; a high-sugar diet compounds long-term risk.
dietary_guidance: Favour a low-sugar, balanced diet during long-term therapy.

mechanism: Additive CNS depression and hypotension.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol.

mechanism: Marked additive sedation and CNS depression; overdose danger.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol.

mechanism: Additive CNS effects and impaired judgement; possible increased GI bleeding risk.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol.

mechanism: Additive CNS effects; hepatic caution with duloxetine.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol; avoid with significant liver disease.

mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol.

mechanism: Less sedating than first-generation but additive impairment still occurs with some agents.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol, especially with cetirizine/levocetirizine.

mechanism: Lithium clearance tracks sodium: a fall in sodium intake raises lithium levels (toxicity); a rise lowers them (loss of effect).
dietary_guidance: Keep sodium intake CONSISTENT day to day; do not start a low-salt diet without monitoring.

mechanism: Caffeine increases lithium renal clearance; stopping caffeine abruptly can raise lithium to toxic levels.
dietary_guidance: Keep caffeine intake steady; change it only with level monitoring.

mechanism: Caffeine is pharmacologically similar to theophylline; additive toxicity (tremor, tachyarrhythmia, seizures).
dietary_guidance: Minimise caffeine while on theophylline-type drugs.

mechanism: Alcohol reduces theophylline clearance and adds to nausea/reflux.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol.

mechanism: Additive tremor, tachycardia and hypokalaemia with large caffeine loads.
dietary_guidance: Limit strong coffee / energy drinks around dosing.

mechanism: Additive CNS and cardiovascular stimulation (tachycardia, hypertension, anxiety, insomnia).
dietary_guidance: Avoid or minimise caffeine.

mechanism: Di/trivalent cations (calcium, iron, zinc, magnesium) chelate fluoroquinolones and can abolish absorption.
dietary_guidance: Separate the dose from dairy, antacids, and iron/calcium/zinc supplements by >=2 hours (6 h ideal).

mechanism: Milk/yoghurt calcium chelates fluoroquinolones (esp. ciprofloxacin, norfloxacin), reducing absorption.
dietary_guidance: Do not take with milk or yoghurt; separate by >=2 hours.

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 and reduces caffeine clearance; jitteriness and insomnia.
dietary_guidance: Cut back on caffeine during the course.

mechanism: Calcium, iron, zinc and magnesium chelate tetracyclines, markedly reducing absorption.
dietary_guidance: Separate from dairy, antacids and mineral supplements by >=2 hours.

mechanism: Milk calcium chelates tetracyclines (classical interaction; doxycycline less affected than older agents).
dietary_guidance: Avoid taking with milk; separate by >=2 hours.

mechanism: Calcium and iron salts bind levothyroxine in the gut and reduce absorption, causing under-treatment.
dietary_guidance: Take levothyroxine fasting; separate calcium/iron by >=4 hours.

mechanism: Soy protein and soy fibre reduce levothyroxine absorption.
dietary_guidance: Separate levothyroxine from soy foods/supplements by >=4 hours; keep soy intake consistent.

mechanism: Cow's milk taken with levothyroxine reduces its absorption.
dietary_guidance: Take levothyroxine with water on an empty stomach, not with milk.

mechanism: Any food, and especially calcium/iron/magnesium, blocks oral bisphosphonate absorption (bioavailability already <1%).
dietary_guidance: Take on waking with plain water only; no food, milk, coffee or supplements for >=30-60 minutes.

mechanism: Milk calcium prevents bisphosphonate absorption.
dietary_guidance: Plain water only with the dose; wait >=30-60 minutes before milk.

mechanism: Long-term acid suppression reduces absorption of calcium carbonate, iron, magnesium and vitamin B12.
dietary_guidance: Use calcium citrate rather than carbonate; monitor magnesium/B12 on long-term use.

mechanism: Iron salts chelate levodopa and carbidopa, reducing absorption; dietary protein also competes for transport.
dietary_guidance: Separate iron supplements from levodopa doses; keep protein distribution consistent.

mechanism: Disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, vomiting, tachycardia) with even small amounts of alcohol, including in sauces/tonics.
dietary_guidance: No alcohol during and for 48-72 hours after the course; check cough syrups and food for alcohol.

mechanism: Cefoperazone and a few other cephalosporins with a methyltetrazolethiol side chain cause a disulfiram-like reaction.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol with cefoperazone-containing products.

mechanism: Disulfiram blocks acetaldehyde breakdown; any alcohol - including in food, sauces, vinegar, mouthwash - triggers a severe reaction.
dietary_guidance: Strictly avoid all sources of alcohol, including hidden ones.

mechanism: Furazolidone (and to a lesser extent nitrofurantoin) can cause a disulfiram-like reaction.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol during the course.

mechanism: Occasional disulfiram-like reactions and additive hepatic stress.
dietary_guidance: Limit or avoid alcohol during the course.

mechanism: Chronic alcohol induces CYP2E1 and depletes glutathione, greatly increasing paracetamol hepatotoxicity even at near-therapeutic doses.
dietary_guidance: Do not exceed 2 g/day paracetamol if drinking regularly; avoid the combination.

mechanism: Additive hepatic stress; caution with heavy or regular alcohol use.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol; report muscle pain or dark urine.

mechanism: Methotrexate plus alcohol markedly raises the risk of hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol, or keep well within conservative limits agreed with the clinician.

mechanism: Additive hepatotoxicity; daily alcohol also alters rifampicin metabolism.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol during therapy.

mechanism: Additive hepatotoxicity; rare disulfiram-like reaction with ketoconazole.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol; avoid with ketoconazole.

mechanism: Ongoing alcohol intake directly opposes the purpose of hepatoprotective therapy.
dietary_guidance: Abstain from alcohol.

mechanism: A high-purine diet raises uric acid production and opposes urate-lowering therapy; may trigger flares.
dietary_guidance: Limit organ meat, red meat, shellfish, meat extracts and yeast extract.

mechanism: Alcohol (especially beer) raises uric acid and precipitates gout flares, working against therapy.
dietary_guidance: Avoid beer and spirits; minimise all alcohol.

mechanism: High purine intake increases the uric acid load the drug must clear; stone risk.
dietary_guidance: Limit high-purine foods; keep fluid intake high.

mechanism: Alcohol precipitates and worsens acute gout attacks.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol during a flare.

mechanism: Both are vasodilators; combined use causes profound hypotension, dizziness and syncope.
dietary_guidance: Avoid alcohol, especially around dosing.

mechanism: High sodium intake blunts antihypertensive efficacy.
dietary_guidance: Keep salt intake moderate.

mechanism: Large caffeine loads can transiently raise blood pressure and offset rate control.
dietary_guidance: Avoid excessive caffeine.

mechanism: Additive vasodilation; first-dose and postural hypotension.
dietary_guidance: Take the first doses at night; limit alcohol.

mechanism: Additive orthostatic hypotension.
dietary_guidance: Rise slowly; limit alcohol.

mechanism: Additive sedation and hypotension.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol.

mechanism: High calcium load can potentiate digoxin effect on the heart; bran/high-fibre meals reduce digoxin absorption.
dietary_guidance: Avoid high-dose calcium; keep fibre intake consistent and separate from the dose.

mechanism: Cimetidine (and to a lesser extent others) inhibits gastric alcohol dehydrogenase, raising blood alcohol.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol, especially with cimetidine.

mechanism: Cimetidine reduces hepatic caffeine clearance.
dietary_guidance: Cut back caffeine if using cimetidine.

mechanism: Both lower blood pressure; combined with alcohol causes dizziness and hypotension.
dietary_guidance: Limit alcohol around dosing.

mechanism: Caffeine is co-formulated with ergotamine to aid absorption; excessive extra caffeine adds to vasoconstriction.
dietary_guidance: Do not add large amounts of caffeine beyond the product itself.

mechanism: Additive vasoconstriction; some combination products already contain caffeine.
dietary_guidance: Avoid excessive caffeine around a migraine dose.

mechanism: Additive activation - jitteriness, raised blood pressure - with venlafaxine at higher doses.
dietary_guidance: Moderate caffeine intake.

mechanism: No specific interaction; heavy alcohol adds to nausea and (with valaciclovir at high dose) renal stress.
dietary_guidance: General moderation; maintain hydration.

mechanism: Protease inhibitors are CYP3A4 substrates/inhibitors; grapefruit can further raise levels.
dietary_guidance: Avoid grapefruit/pomelo with protease-inhibitor regimens.

mechanism: Not a clinically important interaction; documented to note it is generally safe.
dietary_guidance: No restriction beyond consistency.

mechanism: Oral aminoglycosides are barely absorbed; the classical chelation issue does not apply to systemic (IV) use.
dietary_guidance: No dietary action for injectable use.
